outcome: The Mixed Methods Workbench is finished to 1.0 as a general tool and as part of Brian's broader evidence-to-action vision, not for one use case: each study is one investigation record, the investigation spine the repository's evidence-to-action product map describes, running from question and evidence to reviewed findings and next actions; on two rights-clear interview corpora a person can open that record, follow every qualitative claim to its passage, see a quantitative strand measured and checked against the authors' own coding, read a joint display with bounded meta-inferences and a gated causal check, review and export everything with full traces, and read on a benchmark page what works, what fails and what it cost. The public PsychosisBank review stays served from committed files.

entries.criterion: I can open the public review and see, for each finding, what backs it and that no causal conclusion is published yet
demonstration: Open https://psychosisbank-review.brianmills2718.workers.dev/
Scroll to the 'Independent challenge' section and read each finding's card
Click a cited excerpt's source link
entries.expected: Each finding shows its verdict, the source excerpts behind it and the remaining source gap; the page says the causal conclusion is withheld pending researcher review; the source link opens the original public document.
entries.failure_example: Finding 3's quote about 'this level' without its antecedent: a broken page shows the quote alone, with no note that the TalkBank policy names it 'Controlled access'.

representation.note: The router picked a table for one row per finding; the existing page shows the same fields as one card per finding, which reads the same way on a phone. Kept, not rebuilt.

entries.criterion: I can see which method steps the crosswalk found shared across methods, and why
demonstration: Open the crosswalk page (built in slice S7, a table rendered from docs/research/method_decomposition/phase5/adjudication.yaml; until then the file on GitHub)
Read the table of groups, one row per group of steps from two or more methods
Open one row's justification
entries.expected: 36 rows; each says same capability, shared shell or different capability with a one-line reason; today none says same capability.
entries.failure_example: A row with members from one method only, or a verdict with no reason, means the generator or the check is broken.

entries.criterion: I can open the study page for a general example corpus and follow each qualitative claim back to the interview passage it rests on, and see the corpus is frozen with its licence
demonstration: Open the study page's address in the slice report (open question Q11 decides where it is served: hive.brianmills.dev or the PsychosisBank Worker; until he answers, the report links the committed page and carries screenshots)
Read the corpus panel: 26 interviews, licence CC BY-SA 4.0, each file's hash status
Click a category, then one of its supporting passages
Read the passage in its interview, with its speaker and the author's own codes for that span
entries.expected: Every interview shows 'hash matches Zenodo' in blue; each of QC's 8 categories and 6 propositions lists its passages; each passage opens at the right place in the right interview; the quantitative and integration strands say 'not built yet' in grey.
entries.failure_example: A passage whose offsets do not match the frozen text: a broken page shows the wrong words silently; a working page lists it under 'offset mismatches' in orange with both texts.

entries.criterion: I can see one coded theme measured across every interview, and how well that measure agrees with the author's own coding on interviews it was not tuned on
demonstration: Open the study page's Measurement tab (the study page's address in the slice report (open question Q11 decides where it is served: hive.brianmills.dev or the PsychosisBank Worker; until he answers, the report links the committed page and carries screenshots))
Read the feasibility readout and the instrument: which of the author's codes is measured and why (how many of QC's cited turns it holds), its definition, and its included and excluded examples

Read the table of measures: always-majority, word-list count, TF-IDF regression and the language model, each with how often it finds the author's coded turns and how often its finds are right, how far its count of the theme per interview is from the author's, and the range of that count
Read which interviews tuned each measure and which tested it, and the shuffled-label control row with the chance level printed beside it
Click a disagreement and read the turn, the model's quoted reason and the author's code
entries.expected: Every figure names the interviews it was tested on, none of which were used to tune it. The shuffled-label row sits near the chance level printed beside it, and the always-majority row scores no better than its own baseline. The count error per interview is shown beside agreement (never accuracy alone). Every disagreement opens its turn and its model trace. The readout shows why this code was chosen, with the counts ("QC cites 22 turns; the code marks 14 of them and 72 in all"), and every agreement figure carries "one coder, no adjudication, definition drafted from her passages".
entries.failure_example: A build that let tuning see the held-out interviews: the page shows an interview on both the tuned and tested lists in orange and refuses the figure; or the shuffled-label control scores well above chance, shown in orange, which means the measure is reading something other than the construct.

entries.criterion: I can compare each qualitative proposition with the measured numbers, see which ones the measure speaks to and how, and what may be concluded from both together
demonstration: Open the Joint display tab
Read the count of mapped rows at the top (how many of the six propositions the measure speaks to)
Read one row per proposition: the claim, then either the measured figure it is compared with and the verdict, or "silent: not measured" in grey with the reason
Open a mapped row's meta-inference and its number and passage check
entries.expected: The page states how many of the six rows are mapped. A mapped row is matched by prevalence alone, so it shows the verdict word "complements" with the passages and numbers it rests on and a passed number and passage check; the page says why it cannot say converges or diverges. Each other row says "silent: not measured" in grey with its reason; a row whose units differ says aggregation is blocked; every meta-inference says 'pending review' until reviewed.
entries.failure_example: A prevalence-only row marked "converges": the check shows it in orange, says a prevalence cannot confirm a when-then claim, and it cannot be accepted. Or a meta-inference citing a number that is not in the measured result (S6 plants one): the check shows it in orange with the number it could not find. Or every row shows the same measured figure as if each proposition were measured: the mapping is missing.

entries.criterion: I can see a causal check on one proposition kept apart from how common it is, and that no causal conclusion shows unless the gate allows it
demonstration: Open the Causal tab
Read the hypothesis, each evidence test and its verdict
Read the publication gate line
Open 'How the gate behaves' and read both test exports
entries.expected: Process Tracing's within-case verdicts are shown in their own panel, never merged with the prevalence; a conclusion shows only when the gate says publishable, else 'withheld' and why. On the Open Science proposition the export comes from Process Tracing's answer path, which carries no publication gate, so the line reads 'withheld: Process Tracing's answer path carries no publication gate'. In 'How the gate behaves', two made-up test exports, labelled as test data: the one with a publishable gate shows its conclusion, the one with a blocked gate reads 'withheld' and why.
entries.failure_example: A Process Tracing export whose gate is not publishable still shows the causal conclusion; or the publishable test export still reads 'withheld' (a page that never shows any conclusion).

entries.criterion: I can accept, reject or annotate each meta-inference and write a reflexivity memo, see them saved, and download one bundle with every trace
demonstration: Open the study workbench (the study workbench's address in the slice report (open question Q11 decides where it is served: hive.brianmills.dev or the PsychosisBank Worker; until he answers, the report links the committed page and carries screenshots))
Accept one meta-inference and reject another with a note; on the served page each opens a pre-filled GitHub issue to submit (open question Q20), locally the page saves directly
Write a short reflexivity memo in the memo panel and save it the same way
Reload the page (served page: after the next build, which imports the issues)
Click 'Download bundle' and read the page's hash check beside the download
entries.expected: Both decisions and the memo show in the review log and in the bundle; until a served-page decision is imported it shows 'recorded, waiting to be imported' in grey. The bundle's manifest lists every file with its hash, including each run's trace, the memo and the reporting checklist, and the page's own hash check shows every file 'matches' in blue.
entries.failure_example: A decision or memo that vanishes after reload or import, or a bundle file whose hash differs from its manifest line: the page's hash check shows that file 'differs' in orange.

entries.criterion: I can see on two different corpora what the workbench gets right, what it gets wrong, which planted failures it catches, and what each run cost
demonstration: Open the benchmark page
Read one row per corpus and strand: agreement with the authors' coding
Read the planted-failure table
Read cost and time per run with its basis
entries.expected: Both corpora appear; every planted failure is listed as caught (blue) or missed (orange); costs cite their llm-cost measurement.
entries.failure_example: A planted altered quote that the checks pass: the row reads 'missed' in orange, not hidden.

entries.criterion: I can see which methods the finished workbench actually runs and which it does not
demonstration: Open the method-profile page
Filter to 'runs in 1.0'
For one method marked as run, open the slice and the test linked beside it
Read the reason beside an unsupported method
entries.expected: Every method profile carries runs / does not run; each 'runs' links the slice that built it and the test that exercises it; each 'does not run' has a one-line reason; the release notes list both lists.
entries.failure_example: A method marked as run whose slice or test link is missing or opens nothing.

entries.criterion: I can point the workbench at a corpus it has never seen and get the same study page, without anyone changing its code
demonstration: Open the benchmark page's 'corpora' list and the second corpus's study page
Read, for each corpus, the line 'files changed to add this corpus' and open its commit link
Open the second corpus's study definition file (the only file added for it) from its link
entries.expected: The second corpus's study page has the same panels as the first. Its line reads 'data only' in blue (one study definition file plus frozen data). A test works this out from the list of files changed by the commit that added the corpus, not the builder that reads it, and the commit link shows the same file list. The page states which corpus fields were required and which optional, and on what the second corpus differs from the first.
entries.failure_example: A corpus name, file layout or code list written into the workbench's code: the 'files changed' line lists a code path in orange instead of 'data only', and the commit link shows the same path.

entries.criterion: Each study is the investigation record of my broader evidence-to-action vision (the product map's investigation spine): one record I can open that keeps its question, evidence, analytical plan, method runs, findings, unresolved questions, reviews and next actions together, and the PsychosisBank investigation is one of them, not a separate destination
demonstration: Open the workbench's study list (the study workbench's address in the slice report (open question Q11 decides where it is served: hive.brianmills.dev or the PsychosisBank Worker; until he answers, the report links the committed page and carries screenshots))
Open the Open Science study, then the PsychosisBank investigation

In each, read the question and the analytical plan (which strands run, the integration design, the evidence each needs), then follow one finding to its evidence, the method run that produced it and its review decision
Read the unresolved questions and the next actions, and open the product-map link at the top of the record
entries.expected: Both studies open in the same record layout with the same eight parts the product map names (question, evidence, analytical plan, method runs, findings, unresolved questions, reviews, next actions), and the record links that map; each finding links its evidence, its run receipt and its review state; each next action says what it would do with the evidence; the PsychosisBank public page still shows the same content.
entries.failure_example: The PsychosisBank investigation still opens as its own one-off page with a different layout, a finding shows no run or review link, the record has no analytical plan, or it stops at findings with no next actions: it is a report, not the evidence-to-action record.
